notes: This file lists skills that live in other people's GitHub repos. Nothing here is a copy. Each entry says where the skill lives, who made it, its licence, and how to get it on each Claude surface. INSTALL-FOR-CLAUDE.md explains the fields.

groups.core: Writing and everyday skills. 'Get all the skills' means this group.
groups.builtin: Anthropic skills that are already part of the Claude app. Switch them on; nothing to download.
groups.role-packs: Anthropic plugins for a job role. Optional: install only the one for your job.

sets.name: Writing that sounds human
sets.why: Stop Slop keeps Claude's new drafts clean as it writes. Humanizer fixes text that already sounds machine-made. Use Stop Slop for anything Claude writes for you, and Humanizer on anything you're handed.

sets.name: Website copy
sets.why: Find out what customers actually say, write the page in their words, then tighten it. Run them in that order.

sets.name: Email and social
sets.why: Plan a campaign once, then write the email series and the posts that go with it, so both say the same thing.

sets.name: On-brand decks
sets.why: Turn your company's PowerPoint template into a skill, and use Theme Factory to keep colours and fonts consistent on everything else. Switch on Skill Creator for the template step.

sets.name: Diagrams and visuals
sets.why: Diagram Design for processes, org charts and timelines; Canvas Design for posters, flyers and one-page graphics.

sets.name: Your week
sets.why: Run your weekly review, then turn what came out of it into the update your manager or team expects.

skills.name: humanizer
skills.title: Humanizer
skills.author: Siqi Chen
skills.summary: Rewrites text that sounds like AI wrote it so it reads like a person wrote it, without changing what it says. It works from Wikipedia's guide to the signs of AI writing: forced lists of three, 'it's not X, it's Y' lines, puffed-up claims, stock words and one-line closers.
use_when: You drafted an email, post or report with Claude and it sounds like a chatbot.
You want to check someone else's draft for AI tells before it goes out.
skills.try: Use the humanizer skill on this draft. Keep the meaning and the facts exactly as they are.
skills.notes: Overlaps with stop-slop. Both are good; if Claude picks the wrong one, name the one you want.

skills.name: stop-slop
skills.title: Stop Slop
skills.author: Hardik Pandya
skills.summary: A short, strict set of rules for writing that doesn't sound machine-made: cut filler, use active voice, name specific things, vary sentence length, no em dashes. It comes with lists of phrases and sentence shapes to avoid, and scores a draft before handing it back.
use_when: You want Claude to write in a plain, direct voice from the start, not fix it afterwards.
You're editing a draft and want a checklist-style pass.
skills.try: Write a two-paragraph update to the team about the new delivery schedule. Use the stop-slop rules.
skills.notes: Overlaps with humanizer. Stop-slop is stricter and shorter; humanizer explains more.

skills.name: prompt-master
skills.title: Prompt Master
skills.author: Nidhin Joseph Nelson
skills.summary: Writes a tight, ready-to-paste prompt for another AI tool: ChatGPT, Gemini, Midjourney, an image or video tool, and so on. It works out which tool you're aiming at and what you actually want, asks only what it needs, and hands back one prompt.
use_when: You need a prompt for a different AI tool and don't know how that tool likes to be asked.
A prompt you use keeps giving you the wrong thing and you want it fixed.
skills.try: Write me a prompt for Midjourney: a photo-style image of a builders' merchant yard at sunrise for our website banner.
skills.notes: It only switches on when you ask it to write or fix a prompt, so it stays out of the way otherwise.

skills.name: copywriting
skills.title: Copywriting
skills.author: Corey Haines
skills.summary: Writes marketing copy for web pages: home page, landing page, pricing, product and about pages. It asks who the page is for and what they should do next, then writes headlines, sections and calls to action, with options to choose from.
use_when: You're writing or rewriting a page on your website.
You have a page that gets visits but not enquiries and want fresh copy to test.
skills.try: Use the copywriting skill to rewrite the hero section of our trade-account page. Here's the current text: ...
skills.notes: Part of Corey Haines's Marketing Skills collection on GitHub.

skills.name: copy-editing
skills.title: Copy Editing
skills.author: Corey Haines
skills.summary: Edits copy you already have instead of starting over. It goes through the text in several passes (clarity, voice, proof, specifics, flow) and tells you what it changed and why.
use_when: You have a draft brochure, web page or email and want it tightened.
Old marketing text needs a refresh but should keep its structure.
skills.try: Copy-edit this product page. Show me the changes as a list before you rewrite it.

skills.name: emails
skills.title: Email Sequences
skills.author: Corey Haines
skills.summary: Plans and writes a series of emails: welcome emails, follow-ups after a quote, win-back emails for lapsed customers. It sets the order, timing and goal of each email, then writes them.
use_when: You want a set of emails that go out over days or weeks, not a single one.
You're setting up emails in Mailchimp, HubSpot or similar and need the words.
skills.try: Plan a 4-email follow-up sequence for customers who got a quote but didn't order. Then write email 1.

skills.name: social
skills.title: Social Media
skills.author: Corey Haines
skills.summary: Writes and plans posts for LinkedIn, X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook. It knows how each platform differs and can turn one piece of content into a week of posts.
use_when: You need LinkedIn posts from a case study, blog post or announcement.
You want a simple posting plan for the month.
skills.try: Turn this customer story into three LinkedIn posts for our company page. Different angle for each.

skills.name: customer-research
skills.title: Customer Research
skills.author: Corey Haines
skills.summary: Turns raw customer material into findings: interview notes, survey answers, reviews, support tickets. It pulls out the problems, wants and exact phrases customers use, so your copy and decisions use their words.
use_when: You have a pile of reviews, survey results or call notes and want the patterns.
You're about to write marketing copy and want to know how customers describe the problem.
skills.try: Here are 40 customer reviews. Use the customer-research skill: what do customers praise, what do they complain about, and what phrases do they repeat?

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.title: Skill Creator
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Builds new skills with you, and tests and improves the ones you have. It interviews you about the task, writes the skill, and can run it with and without the skill to show the difference.
use_when: You want to turn a task you do every week into a skill (Lesson 7).
A skill you built isn't doing what you want and needs fixing.
skills.try: I want to build a skill. Interview me about how I write our monthly customer newsletter.
skills.notes: In the Claude app it's listed under Customize > Skills as a skill from Anthropic. Switch it on there.

skills.name: docx
skills.title: Word documents
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: How Claude makes and edits Word files: headings, tables, page numbers, tracked changes, letterheads. In the Claude app it's already on and loads by itself whenever you ask for a Word document.
use_when: You ask for a report, letter, policy or proposal as a .docx.
You upload a Word file and want it edited, with changes tracked.
skills.try: Make this into a two-page Word document with a title page and a table of contents.
skills.notes: Anthropic's licence for this skill does not allow copies outside Claude. Don't download or re-share it; use it where Anthropic provides it.

skills.name: xlsx
skills.title: Excel spreadsheets
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: How Claude reads, cleans and builds spreadsheets with working formulas, formatting and charts. Already on in the Claude app.
use_when: You upload a spreadsheet and want it analysed, fixed or reformatted.
You want a new tracker, budget or price list as a real Excel file.
skills.try: Build me an Excel tracker for supplier deliveries with a column for days late that calculates itself.
skills.notes: Same licence as the Word skill: use it inside Claude, don't copy it.

skills.name: pptx
skills.title: PowerPoint decks
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: How Claude makes and edits PowerPoint decks, including working from your own template. Already on in the Claude app.
use_when: You need a deck from notes, a report or a meeting summary.
You want an existing deck updated or reworked.
skills.try: Turn this quarterly report into a 6-slide PowerPoint for the leadership meeting.
skills.notes: Same licence as the Word skill: use it inside Claude, don't copy it.

skills.name: pdf
skills.title: PDF files
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: How Claude reads, splits, merges and fills in PDFs, and pulls text and tables out of them. Already on in the Claude app.
use_when: You need the tables out of a supplier PDF and into a spreadsheet.
You want PDFs merged, split or a form filled in.
skills.try: Pull the price table out of this PDF catalogue and put it in a spreadsheet.
skills.notes: Same licence as the Word skill: use it inside Claude, don't copy it.

skills.name: internal-comms
skills.title: Internal Comms
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Writes the messages that go around a company: status reports, leadership updates, project updates, newsletters, FAQs and incident reports. It comes with example formats, including 'Progress, Plans, Problems' updates.
use_when: You owe your manager a weekly update.
Something went wrong and you need a clear incident write-up.
skills.try: Write this week's project update in Progress, Plans, Problems format from these notes: ...
skills.notes: Its examples come from Anthropic's own company. Tell it your format once and it will follow yours.

skills.name: theme-factory
skills.title: Theme Factory
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Gives decks, documents and pages a consistent look. It has ten ready-made colour and font themes, shows them to you as a sample sheet, and can make a new theme to match what you describe.
use_when: Your deck or report works but looks plain.
You want several documents to look like they belong together.
skills.try: Show me the themes, then apply the one that suits a construction supplier to this deck.
skills.notes: For your own company's look, build a brand skill instead (Lesson 7, Demo 4).

skills.name: canvas-design
skills.title: Canvas Design
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Makes one-page visual pieces as PNG or PDF: posters, flyers, simple graphics. It picks a design direction first, then builds the piece to match, with a set of fonts included.
use_when: You need a poster for the staff room or a flyer for an open day.
You want a simple graphic without opening a design tool.
skills.try: Design an A4 poster for our trade open day on 14 March, 7am to 11am, free breakfast.
skills.notes: It's the largest download in the pack because of the fonts it carries.

skills.name: discernment-nudge
skills.title: Discernment Nudge
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: After Claude gives you an answer you might act on (advice, a plan, numbers, a claim), it adds two or three short questions to help you check it: what to verify, where the reasoning could be weak, what context it might be missing.
use_when: You use Claude for decisions, estimates or facts you'll repeat to others.
You're new to AI and want help building the habit of checking its work.
skills.try: Estimate how many extra delivery drivers we need if orders go up 20% in spring.
skills.notes: It runs by itself after big answers. Switch it off if you find the questions get in the way.

skills.name: weekly-review
skills.title: Weekly Review
skills.author: Alireza Rezvani
skills.summary: Walks you through a weekly review based on David Allen's Getting Things Done: clear out loose notes and inboxes, check your task lists, calendar and the things you're waiting on, then look ahead. It ends with one clear next action and a health check on how much you've taken on.
use_when: It's Friday afternoon and you want to close the week with nothing hanging over you.
You've let your task list slide and want to get back on top of it.
You feel you've said yes to too much and want to see what to drop or hand back.
skills.notes: Part of Alireza Rezvani's large Claude Skills collection on GitHub. It works best when you paste in or attach your task list, calendar and notes. Set aside 60 to 90 minutes.
skills.try: Run my weekly review. Here are my task list, this week's calendar and my notes: ...

skills.name: diagram-design
skills.title: Diagram Design
skills.author: Cathryn Lavery
skills.summary: Draws clean, branded diagrams: flowcharts, process maps with swimlanes, org charts, timelines, Gantt charts, customer journeys, funnels, two-by-two grids and simple charts. It saves them as a web page or image you can drop into a document or deck.
use_when: You need to show how a process works, who hands what to whom.
You want an org chart or project timeline that looks finished, not hand-drawn.
A plan is easier to explain as a picture than as paragraphs.
skills.notes: The first time you use it, it asks for your brand colours (you can give it your website address). Keep each diagram to a handful of boxes: it's built to leave things out rather than cram them in.
skills.try: Draw a swimlane diagram of our quote-to-invoice process: sales takes the enquiry, ops checks stock, finance raises the invoice ...

skills.name: ppt-template-creator
skills.title: PowerPoint Template Creator
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Turns your company's PowerPoint template into a skill of its own. Give it your .pptx or .potx file and it studies the layouts and where everything sits, then builds a skill that makes on-brand decks from that template every time.
use_when: Claude's decks don't match your company look and you want them to.
You make the same kind of deck often (board packs, client proposals, monthly reviews) and want it on your template without fixing it by hand.
skills.notes: It makes a skill, not a deck. When it's done, upload the new skill like any other (Customize > Skills), then ask for decks as usual. It uses Skill Creator along the way, so switch that on too. It comes from Anthropic's financial-services collection but works for any company template.
skills.try: Use the ppt-template-creator skill to turn this template into a skill for our company decks. [attach your .pptx or .potx]

skills.name: productivity
skills.title: Productivity (plugin)
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Helps you plan the day, keep a task list and build up notes about your work that Claude remembers between sessions. Works best in Cowork, connected to your calendar and email.
use_when: You start each day by working out what matters.
You want Claude to keep track of people, projects and open tasks for you.
skills.try: /productivity:start
skills.notes: A plugin is a bundle of skills (and sometimes connectors). Install it from Customize > Plugins.

skills.name: brand-voice
skills.title: Brand Voice (plugin)
skills.author: Tribe AI
skills.summary: Works out your company's voice from documents you already have (past emails, proposals, call notes), writes brand guidelines from them, then checks new writing against those guidelines.
use_when: Your company has no written style guide and you want one.
Several people write customer-facing text and it all sounds different.
skills.try: Generate brand voice guidelines from these five proposals and our website text.
skills.notes: Built by Tribe AI and published in Anthropic's plugin collection.

skills.name: marketing
skills.title: Marketing (plugin)
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Campaign plans, content drafts, email sequences, competitor briefs, SEO checks and performance reports, plus a brand review of anything before it goes out.
use_when: Marketing is your job, or a big part of it.
You want campaign planning and reporting as well as writing.
skills.try: Plan a spring campaign for our trade customers: goals, channels, timeline and first drafts.
skills.notes: Overlaps with Corey Haines's marketing skills in the core group. Use one set or the other for writing.

skills.name: sales
skills.title: Sales (plugin)
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Account research, call prep, call summaries with follow-up emails, pipeline and deal reviews, and outreach drafts. Gets more useful when it's connected to your CRM.
use_when: You prepare for sales calls and write follow-ups.
You review a pipeline or forecast each week.
skills.try: Prep me for a call with Hendricks Construction tomorrow. Here's what I know: ...
skills.notes: The call-summary skill doubles as a meeting-notes skill for any call.

skills.name: customer-support
skills.title: Customer Support (plugin)
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Sorts and prioritises tickets, drafts replies, writes escalation notes and turns solved problems into help articles.
use_when: You answer customer emails or tickets.
The same questions keep coming in and you want help articles for them.
skills.try: Draft a reply to this complaint and tell me if it should be escalated.

skills.name: operations
skills.title: Operations (plugin)
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Process write-ups, status reports, risk assessments, vendor reviews, change requests and capacity plans.
use_when: You need to write down how a process works so someone else can run it.
You compare suppliers or plan for a busy season.
skills.try: Write up our goods-in process as a step-by-step document from these notes.

skills.name: human-resources
skills.title: Human Resources (plugin)
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Job offers, interview plans, onboarding plans, performance review drafts, policy look-ups and people reports.
use_when: You hire, onboard or review staff.
People ask you policy questions you answer from the handbook.
skills.try: Build a first-week onboarding plan for a new warehouse supervisor.
skills.notes: Check anything about pay, contracts or employment law with a person before you act on it.

skills.name: finance
skills.title: Finance (plugin)
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Month-end close, reconciliations, journal entries, variance analysis and financial statements, for in-house finance teams.
use_when: You work in accounts or finance and do a monthly close.
You need to explain why this month's numbers differ from budget.
skills.try: Explain the main variances between budget and actual in this spreadsheet.
skills.notes: Built for accountants. A finance person should check its work.

skills.name: legal
skills.title: Legal (plugin)
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Contract review, NDA triage, compliance checks and meeting briefings, for in-house legal teams.
use_when: You review supplier contracts or NDAs before they go to a lawyer.
You need a quick list of the risky clauses in a document.
skills.try: Review this supplier contract and list the clauses we should push back on.
skills.notes: It helps you prepare. It is not legal advice; a lawyer still signs off.

skills.name: small-business
skills.title: Small Business (plugin)
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Everyday jobs for owners of small firms: chasing invoices, cash-flow snapshots, proposals, job adverts, review replies, month-end prep and a Monday briefing.
use_when: You run a small business and cover several roles yourself.
You want one plugin instead of separate sales, finance and HR ones.
skills.try: Give me a cash-flow snapshot from this bank export and list the invoices I should chase.
skills.notes: It's a large plugin with many skills. If Claude picks the wrong one, name the one you want.

skills.name: product-management
skills.title: Product Management (plugin)
skills.author: Anthropic
skills.summary: Feature specs, roadmap updates, stakeholder updates, competitor briefs and summaries of user research.
use_when: You own a product or service and write specs or roadmaps.
You have interview notes or survey results to turn into findings.
skills.try: Write a one-page spec for adding online ordering for trade customers.
